summary: The candidate adds an opt-in contract and reducer tests, but the real Cosmos3 candidate path fails during latent creation because a per-candidate generator list is passed to torch.randn and the latent batch dimension remains one.

tests.command: PYTHONPATH=python /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-7ca1fa9a783f/venv/bin/python - <<'PY' ... base contract import check ... PY
tests.what_was_measured: On the recorded base, SamplingParams lacks candidate_trajectory and the candidate contract module cannot be imported.
Candidate-provided focused unit/regression suite: 153 tests and 43 subtests passed.
Actual Cosmos3LatentPreparationStage with one conditioning observation and two independently seeded generators fails at torch.randn(generator=list); conditioning/noise batch dimension is also one.
Standalone candidate GPU arithmetic check on MI350X; deterministic draws matched and mean error versus CPU float64 reference was 1.1920928955078125e-07, but no Cosmos3 pipeline code executed.

gpu_execution.evidence: One AMD Instinct MI350X executed the candidate's standalone RNG/reducer script under Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 and HIP 7.2.26015; this was not an end-to-end model or pipeline validation.

remaining_counterexamples: Cosmos3LatentPreparationStage passes the list of per-candidate generators to torch.randn, which raises TypeError before denoising.
For one conditioning image, Cosmos3LatentPreparationStage chooses batch_dim=1 rather than candidate count, so it does not construct the promised physical candidate batch.
remaining_limitations: Cosmos3 action model weights were unavailable, so end-to-end serving and semantic action quality were not tested.
TP/SP, CFG, cancellation/failure recovery, dynamic co-batching, and N={1,2,4,8,10} performance benchmarks were not exercised.
No native source changed; a native rebuild was not applicable.
